title: Effects of 16 weeks of pyramidal and polarized training intensity distributions in well-trained endurance runners
authors: Filipas L, Bonato M, Gallo G, Codella R
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
population: Sixty well-trained male runners, 16-week intervention with training load kept constant
findings: Four groups: pyramidal (PYR), polarized (POL), PYR then POL (8+8 weeks) and POL then PYR.
Significant group x time interactions for relative VO2peak (p<0.0001), velocity at 2 and 4 mmol/L lactate (both p<0.0001) and 5 km time trial (p=0.0001).
PYR then POL improved most: about 3.0% relative VO2peak, 1.7% vBLa2, 1.5% vBLa4 and 1.5% 5 km time trial.
Every intervention improved surrogates and performance in well-trained runners.
limitations: Male only, single research group, 16 weeks, load matched by design so volume effects untested. Goal event was 5 km; not tested for marathon or ultra.
implications: Supports phase-based TID for 5-10 km goals: pyramidal early, polarized in the later specific block (consistent with Casado 2022).
Hold total load constant when switching TID; change the distribution, not the volume, at the transition.
Do not generalise the shift to marathon/ultra goals without other evidence.

verification.notes: Crossref: published online 2021-11-25, print 2022-03; journal and first author match. Numbers confirmed in abstract.
